source_text: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus. Has martyrum coelestes coronas, has confessorum glorias spiritales, has stantium fratrum maximas eximiasque virtutes moestitia una contristat, quod avulsam nostrorum viscerum partem violentus inimicus populationis suae strage dejecit. Quid hoc loco faciam, dilectissimi fratres? fluctuans vario mentis aestu, quid aut quomodo dicam? Lacrymis magis quam verbis opus est ad exprimendum dolorem quo corporis nostri plaga deflenda est, quo populi aliquando numerosi multiplex lamentanda jactura est. Quis enim sic durus aut ferreus, quis sic fraternae charitatis oblitus, qui inter suorum multiformes ruinas et lugubres ac multo squalore deformes reliquias constitutus siccos oculos tenere praevaleat, nec, erumpente statim fletu, prius gemitus suos lacrymis quam voce depromat? Doleo, fratres, doleo vobiscum, nec mihi ad leniendos dolores meos integritas propria et sanitas privata blanditur, quando plus pastor in gregis sui vulnere vulneretur. Cum singulis pectus meum copulo, moeroris et funeris pondera luctuosa participo. Cum plangentibus plango, cum deflentibus defleo, cum jacentibus jacere me credo. Jaculis illis grassantis inimici mea simul membra percussa sunt, saevientes gladii per mea viscera transierunt. Immunis et liber a persecutionis incursu fuisse non potest animus. In prostratis fratribus et me prostravit affectus.
pass_a_gloss: Behold, most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless, our security has been restored by divine aid and vengeance. Minds return to joy, and with the storm of oppression and cloud dispersed, tranquility and serenity have shone forth. Praises must be given to God, and His benefits and gifts must be celebrated with thanksgiving, although our voice did not cease to give thanks even in persecution. For the enemy is not able to prevent those who love the Lord with all their heart and soul and strength from always and everywhere praising His blessings and praises with glory. The day longed for by all has come, and after the horrible and dark night, the world has shone forth radiant with the Lord's light. We look upon the confessors, renowned for their good name and glorious for their virtues and faith, with joyful gazes, clinging to them with holy kisses, embracing those long desired with insatiable longing. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers is present, who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of persecution with a stable confrontation, prepared for the patience of prison, armed for the tolerance of death. You resisted the world strongly, you presented a glorious spectacle to God, you were an example to subsequent brothers. The religious voice spoke Christ, in whom it confessed to have once believed. Illustrious hands, which were accustomed only to divine works, resisted sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly foods, after the body and blood of the Lord, rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your head remained free from the impious and wicked veil, with which the heads of the captives were veiled. Your forehead, with the sign of God, pure, could not bear the devil's crown, it reserved itself for the Lord's crown. How the mother Church joyfully receives you, returning from battle! How blessed, how rejoicing, she opens her gates, so that you may enter with gathered troops, bringing back trophies from the prostrate enemy! Women come with the triumphant men, who, fighting with the world, also overcame their sex. The virgins also come, with double glory of their military service, and boys, who surpassed their years with virtues. The rest of the multitude of the standing also follows your glory, with nearby and almost connected signs of praise, they accompany your footsteps. The same sincerity of heart, the same tenacity of faith, is in them. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, nor destined torments, nor losses of family, nor bodily punishments. Days were being tested for the proof of faith. But he who remembers that he has renounced the world, knows no day of the world; nor does he who hopes for eternity from God now compute earthly times. No one, most beloved brothers, no one must mutilate this glory, no one must weaken the incorrupt firmness of the standing with malignant detraction. When the day appointed for those who denied has passed, whoever has not professed within the day has confessed himself to be a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord apprehended by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step of glory is to be reserved for the Lord by cautious secession. The former is public, the latter private confession. The former conquers the judge of the world, the latter, content with his own judge God, keeps a pure conscience with the integrity of heart. There, fortitude is more prompt, here solicitude is more secure. There, he who was approaching his hour was already found mature; here, perhaps, he who was delayed, having abandoned his patrimony, seceded because he was not going to deny; he would have confessed, certainly, if he had also been detained. These heavenly crowns of martyrs, these spiritual glories of confessors, these greatest and most excellent virtues of standing brothers, one sorrow afflicts, because the violent enemy has thrown down a torn part of our bowels with the destruction of his population. What shall I do in this place, most beloved brothers? Fluctuating with a varied storm of mind, what or how shall I say? Tears are needed more than words to express the grief with which the wound of our body must be lamented, with which the multiple loss of a once numerous people must be mourned. For who is so hard or iron-like, who is so forgetful of fraternal charity, who, established among the many and mournful ruins and lugubrious and very squalid remnants of his own, can prevail in keeping dry eyes, and not, with tears bursting forth immediately, first pour out his groans in tears rather than in voice? I grieve, brothers, I grieve with you, nor does my own integrity and private health flatter me in alleviating my griefs, when the shepherd is more wounded in the wound of his flock. My heart is joined with each one, I participate in the mournful weights of sorrow and funeral. I mourn with those who mourn, I lament with those who lament, I believe I am lying down with those who are lying down. The darts of the raging enemy have struck my limbs at the same time, savage swords have passed through my bowels. The mind could not be immune and free from the attack of persecution. In the prostrate brothers, affection has also prostrated me.

pass_b_english: Most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless only a short time ago—our security—has been rebuilt by God's help and judgment. Our minds return to joy; now that the storm of oppression has blown over and the cloud has scattered, tranquility and serenity shine forth once more. We must give praise to God and celebrate his benefits and gifts with thanksgiving, even though our voice never stopped giving thanks even during the persecution. After all, the enemy cannot prevent those who love the Lord with all their heart, soul, and strength from proclaiming his blessings and praises with glory always and everywhere. The day that everyone longed for has arrived, and after the horrible, dark gloom of a long night, the world has blazed forth, radiant with the Lord's light.

We look upon the confessors—renowned for their good name and glorious for their virtues and faith—with joyful eyes, clinging to them with holy kisses, embracing those we have longed for with an insatiable desire. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers stands here, men who broke the fierce, turbulent fury of persecution by standing their ground, ready for the endurance of prison, armed for the endurance of death. You resisted the world bravely; you offered a glorious spectacle to God; you became an example for the brothers who would follow. A religious voice spoke Christ, confessing that it had believed in him once and for all. Illustrious hands, accustomed only to divine works, refused to take part in sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, having received the body and blood of the Lord, rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your heads remained free of the impious, wicked veil that covered the heads of the captive sacrificers. Your foreheads, marked pure with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown; they reserved themselves for the Lord's crown. How joyfully Mother Church welcomes you as you return from battle! How blessed and rejoicing she is as she opens her gates so that you may enter with gathered ranks, bringing back trophies from the prostrate enemy!

Women come alongside the triumphant men, women who, fighting against the world, also overcame their sex. Virgins come too, bearing the double glory of their military service, and boys who surpassed their years through virtue. The rest of the great multitude of those who stood firm follows your glory as well; with signs of praise close to your own and almost joined to them, they walk in your footsteps. The same sincerity of heart and the same tenacious integrity of faith are in them. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by the traditions of the Gospel, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, destined torments, loss of property, or bodily punishments. The days for testing faith had been set. But the one who remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; nor does the one who hopes for eternity from God calculate earthly times any longer.

No one, most beloved brothers—no one must mutilate this glory; no one must weaken the incorrupt firmness of those who stood firm with malicious detraction. When the appointed day for those who denied had passed, whoever had not confessed within that day confessed himself to be a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord seized by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step toward glory is to be kept safe for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. The former is public confession, the latter private. The former conquers the judge of the world; the latter, content with God as his judge, guards a pure conscience with integrity of heart. There, fortitude is more prompt; here, caution is more secure. There, the man whose hour was approaching was already found mature; here, perhaps the one who was delayed, having abandoned his patrimony, withdrew because he was not going to deny—he certainly would have confessed if he had also been detained.

A single sorrow afflicts these heavenly crowns of martyrs, these spiritual glories of confessors, these greatest and most excellent virtues of the brothers who stood firm: the violent enemy has cast down a torn part of our very bowels through the slaughter of his rampage. What am I to do here, most beloved brothers? My mind tossed by a varied storm, what can I say, or how can I say it? Tears are needed more than words to express the grief with which we must lament the wound of our body, and mourn the manifold loss of a once numerous people. For who is so hard or iron-hearted, who has so forgotten fraternal charity, that standing amid the multiform ruins and the mournful, squalid remnants of his own, he can keep his eyes dry, and not, with tears bursting forth at once, pour out his groans first in tears rather than in voice? I grieve, brothers; I grieve with you. My own integrity and private health do not comfort me in alleviating my griefs, when the shepherd is wounded more deeply in the wound of his flock. My heart is joined to each one of you; I share the mournful weights of sorrow and funeral. I mourn with those who mourn, I lament with those who lament, I feel that I lie down with those who lie down. The darts of the raging enemy have struck my limbs at the same time; savage swords have passed through my bowels. The mind cannot be immune and free from the onslaught of persecution. In my fallen brothers, affection has laid me low as well.
